#### What this PR does / why we need it:
Fix [mount point may become local volume after node rebooting](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/117513) under old volume reconstruction implementation.

During reconstruction, we should not mark volume and device as mounted in ASW, because if there are Pods that use the same volume exist in DSW, they won't get mounted anymore. 

Instead, we should mark the volume state as Uncertain, which meas it will be unmounted for the deleted Pods and mounted for the running Pods during the following reconcile process.

[`NewVolumeManagerReconstruction` also mark volumes on the host as _uncertain_.](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.28.1/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconstruct_new.go#L105) This can make sure that volumes on the host must be mounted/unmounted to get into certain state. Mark them as mounted actually cannot make sure that they get unmounted in the case I described.

> NewVolumeManagerReconstruction also mark volumes on the host as uncertain.

Yes, but at that time reconciler is not running, ASW is empty and thus it's easier to judge consequences. I don't want to say that marking them uncertain in the old reconstruction is wrong, it's just much more risky and test coverage is not great in these parts.
/assign @jingxu97

It should be possible to create an e2e test for this.

* We have tests that restart kubelet and force delete a pod while kubelet is down: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/887ac275a2cfb6030df80bbe3066609336fa220a/test/e2e/storage/testsuites/disruptive.go#L158-L160

* We have csi-mock tests that install a mock CSI driver and can check that NodeStage / NodeUnstage (and any other CSI method) is called: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/887ac275a2cfb6030df80bbe3066609336fa220a/test/e2e/storage/csi_mock/csi_node_stage_error_cases.go#L228-L235

By combining these two, you should be able to create a test that runs a pod with CSI mock driver, shut down kubelet, force-delete the pod, create a replacement pod on the same node, start kubelet and check that NodeStage is called -> the bug is fixed. AFAIK it does not really matter that the test does not really unmount the volume when kubelet is down nor reboot the node - your PR will mark the volume as uncertain anyway and NodeStage should be called in all cases.

It won't be an easy one, but at least the building blocks are there. And it will prove that it actually fixes the issue and prevents further regressions in this area.
@jsafrane Agree to your comment. Let me add an e2e test for the scenario.

issue_context.title: Mount point will be local volume without calling `NodeStageVolume` if mount point was left over before node rebooting
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

The problem can be reproduced by following steps:
1. Create a cluster with one Node
2. Create a deployment with one replica using Non-attachable volume (for example Azurefile) 
3. Shutdown the Node
4. Delete the Pod with option `--force` (Use force deletion to simulate the situation that mount point was left over while original Pod is not in DSW during reconstruction.)
5. Bring back the Node
6. The new Pod is Running on the same Node but it is actually using local mount point.

### What did you expect to happen?

The new Pod should remount to original remote mount point, instead of local mount point.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

As described above.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

The problem is mainly because during volume reconstruction, the reconstructed volume is no longer exists in DSW(since it was force deleted). And  the volume will be added to ASW as `DeviceGloballyMounted`, which actually is not in that state. And then, there is a new Pod created by deployment which will use the same volume, so the volume will be added to DSW. The result is that kubelet will only call `NodePublishVolume` for the new Pod, but not `NodeStageVolume`, which will lead the Pod to use the stale global mount point.
This issue is the same situation as described in this comment: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/116134#issuecomment-1500757052. cc @jsafrane
cc @andyzhangx
so if user does not use force delete pod, it would be safe? @cvvz
I used force delete for simulation, I have no idea whether it can be reproduced in any other way. At least if we don't use force deletion, the problem won't happen.
/triage accepted
@cvvz Could you please try to reproduce this in the latest K8s version?  We want to know whether this is already fixed.
/triage needs-information

This issue should still exist in the latest version under the old reconstruction implementation. 
I don't know whether it can be fixed with `NewVolumeManagerReconstruction` feature enabled. I will test with the feature gate on.

> I used force delete for simulation, I have no idea whether it can be reproduced in any other way. At least if we don't use force deletion, the problem won't happen.

I found another way to reproduce this issue without using `--force` delete is to use pods without controller and pod's restartPolicy is set to  `Never`. 

To reproduce the issue:
1. create cluster with one node
2. create one such pod (no controller & restartPolicy: Never) using azurefile volume
3. reboot the node
4. create another pod with different name using the same azurefile volume while the node is still rebooting
5. the new pod becomes running but using local mount point 

During my test I also found the restartPolicy on the 1st pod is very important. If it's set to `Always`, Kubelet will still call NodeStageVolume to restore the global mount point. however when it's set to `Never`, kubelet skips NodeStageVolume.

> I used force delete for simulation, I have no idea whether it can be reproduced in any other way. At least if we don't use force deletion, the problem won't happen.

4. after the volume is reconstructed by [this point](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconstruct.go#L103), recover the apiserver.

If we change the method of [this line](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconstruct.go#L163) to `MarkDeviceAsUncertain`, can it fix the issue without any side effects on the normal functions of kubelet?

Can you try with Kubernetes 1.28? Or with 1.27 + `NewVolumeManagerReconstruction` feature gate enabled? (Beware of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/117745 then)

review_comments: BTW, even with this fixed, I am quite hesitant to merge it and esp. backport it to older releases. There is a reason we reworked the reconstruction completely.

> This will overwrite possible certain mount in ASW. We've been trying not do that if possible.

This will only mark the volume that is NOT in DSW during reconstruction. So, no matter it is marked as mounted or uncertain, the reconcile will unmount the volume for us, this PR didn't change any behavior.

Since we are handling the volume that is NOT in DSW, the situation here is much clear than PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/110670#:~:text=It%20adds%20volumes,in%20step%231, which aims to fix: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/96635#issuecomment-1145286675 

It marked volume as uncertain by `CheckAndMarkVolumeAsUncertainViaReconstruction` / `CheckAndMarkDeviceUncertainViaReconstruction ` and set [foundDuringReconstruction](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.27.4/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/cache/actual_state_of_world.go#L246) field in ASW, to avoid the volume be marked as `unmounted` again.

However, in our situation, the volume that is NOT is DSW should get unmounted anyway, no matter it is marked as `uncertain `or `mounted`, and [if unmount operation fails, the volume will be marked as uncertain as well](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.27.4/pkg/volume/util/operationexecutor/operation_generator.go#L854-L876).

The only difference is that when multiple pod volumes share the same global mount point, and only some Pods are deleted and not in DSW during reconstruction, `MarkDeviceAsUncertain` will trigger [`MountDevice`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.27.4/pkg/volume/util/operationexecutor/operation_generator.go#L637-L659) in the following reconcile, whereas `MarkDeviceAsMounted` will not, which causes the Pods that are not deleted bind mount to the local global mount.

Let's also take a look at what will happen if `MountDevice`/`UnmountDevice` fails:
* [When `MountDevice` fails, the state will be neither marked as `Uncertain` or `UnMounted`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.27.4/pkg/volume/util/operationexecutor/operation_generator.go#L777-L798), which is ok since our target is to mount device anyway.
* [When `UnmountDevice` fails, the state will be marked as `Uncertain` as well](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.27.4/pkg/volume/util/operationexecutor/operation_generator.go#L957-L969)

Yeah so concern is not that volume was *not* in DSW when it was evaluated and added to ASOW, but in older reconciler, reconstruction and other operations can proceed concurrently and hence we could undo an operation that just finished.
Please check the volume is really uncertain and not certain (applies also to tests below)
